## Summary Add a Mooncake backend on top of the AuxOutput implementation merged in #45635. This PR targets `main` and does not include the legacy commit stack. It promotes the validated implementation reviewed in aoshen02/vllm#7 upstream. Duplicate check: no open upstream PR implements this keys-only R3 storage backend. #57966/#57025 concern prefix omission/KV-offload compatibility, not publishing complete R3 to Mooncake for external retrieval. The fork PR is the earlier review copy, not a separate upstream proposal. ```text GPU worker R3 -> existing background writer -> Mooncake full blocks EngineCore -> clip accepted boundaries -> Mooncake boundary/tail objects TITO HTTP -> ordered aux_output_keys only trainer -> get(keys), concatenate -> complete R3 ``` - Reuse native Mooncake batch I/O, existing configuration/setup and background writer. SHM remains the default. - Return keys on the terminal TITO response, including stored partial tails; no inline R3 with Mooncake. Publication completes before exposing final keys. Requests with string stops publish incremental keys internally so API-side termination can deliver complete R3; HTTP still exposes keys only at completion. - Share full-block keys across instances and DP ranks using block hash and reset generation. P/D must use the same generation, model/R3 profile, hash configuration/seed, block size and Mooncake store. - No new RPC, ACK protocol, publisher thread, TTL registry or retry state. Retention is deployment-owned; missing/evicted objects fail explicitly. - EngineCore owns a separate client for boundaries finalized after Scheduler stop/length handling. Scheduler shutdown closes it; closing the Worker client in another process cannot release it. This does not delete remote objects. ## Validation Local tests: **128 distinct tests passed** across these suites/tests: ```bash python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing -q python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py::test_mooncake_decode_crosses_blocks_and_clips_terminal_output tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q ``` Commands used `/home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python`. A combined run initially had one missing offline default-model snapshot; rerunning that config test in the normal cache environment passed. Changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passes. On this `main`-based branch, reruns passed **92 store/config tests + 34 TITO/IPC tests**, and all changed-file hooks. The new worktree initially lacked local FlashAttention extension links; collection passed after reusing the same installed extensions as the earlier worktree, without source changes. The additional command passed 3 tests (one store rerun and two collector cases). Tests cover the renamed `aux_output_keys` field through IPC, aggregation, streaming/non-streaming HTTP, absence of the old HTTP field, and client close. An attempted full OutputProcessor suite had 10 passes and 33 fixture errors in offline mode; an online retry confirmed HTTP 401 for the gated `meta-llama/Llama-3.2-1B` fixture. That full suite is **not** claimed passing. Slurm GB200 validation: two independent DP4/TP1/EP vLLM instances on two nodes, one shared Mooncake master, RDMA, async scheduling and prefix caching. Consumers run on the opposite node and fetch complete R3 using only returned keys. - 256K context, concurrency32 per instance: cold raw-data equality, hot prefix equality and fresh-client reads after requests finish pass (job30127). - MTP rejection and real stop clipping:32outputs match same-execution raw request/token-position data; fresh reads pass (job30130). - Forced preemption:88preemptions per instance,256requests total, all raw-position and fresh-reader checks pass, including local replay (job30144). Earlier runs with zero preemptions were rejected, not counted as coverage. - Matched SHM/Mooncake end-to-end throughput includes full cross-host retrieval and validation, two rounds,256K/concurrency32 per instance (jobs30115/30131): | Backend | Combined workload-span throughput | | --- | ---: | | SHM |115,758tokens/s | | Mooncake |115,038tokens/s | Difference **-0.62%**, including instance start skew. Averaging summed individual instance rates gives **-0.34%**. No material regression observed in these runs; two rounds are not a confidence interval or a precise intrinsic overhead estimate. Actual weights were **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base**, despite a0731served alias. GPU tests used a pinned-image Python port of the change, not a full target-revision rebuild. Correctness hooks were disabled for throughput measurements. RDMA results do not establish TCP stress reliability; high-key-count TCP reads previously encountered native transport resource exhaustion. The raw oracle checks accepted same-position provenance, not a specific replay version. These GPU runs precede the API-field rename; the rename was validated locally, not with another GPU throughput run. AI assistance was used for implementation and validation; five independent Claude audit rounds of the preceding implementation concluded APPROVE; this follow-up naming/lifecycle review was self-audited. Human line-by-line review and acceptance of the test evidence remain required before merge. ## Multi-turn scaling follow-up (2026-09-21) GB200, actual DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base weights, DP4/TP1/EP per deployment, 256K initial context, 32 concurrent conversations per deployment, four turns (16 generated tokens + 1024 appended input tokens per turn). Prefix caching, chunked prefill and async scheduling enabled. Full R3 is fetched and validated on another node every turn; timing includes retrieval, decoding and validation. Median request-turns/s over three repetitions: | Engine replicas / concurrent conversations | SHM | Mooncake, 4 readers/deployment | Change | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 4 / 32 | 0.623869 | 0.750283 | +20.3% | | 16 / 128 | 2.410555 | 2.954281 | +22.6% | The single-reader control did **not** outperform SHM (0.618058 / 2.361755). Independent native reader clients reduce client-side serialization; this is not an unconditional backend speedup. Each additional reader costs 128 MiB of local transfer buffer. At four deployments, configured Mooncake capacity is 256 GiB versus 128 GiB SHM, so this is not an equal-memory-cost comparison. Backend order was Mooncake then SHM, not randomized; three repeats do not establish statistical significance. Synthetic fixed-token conversations measure serving performance, not model quality. Jobs 30153/30154 completed successfully. Across the 18 phases (including the single-reader control), all 5,760 request-turns passed shape/dtype, output-token and within-conversation cached-prefix R3 equality checks. No preemptions occurred in this performance run; preemption/raw-oracle coverage is reported separately above. This does not assert cross-run, cross-backend bitwise R3 equality. Reproduction configuration: pinned image `vllm/vllm-openai@sha256:95569a195dfe088c22983b08509e8e7156c26b356726147db4072600cba416ed`, image revision `2671fedfc7ae604761990603fc736c0c4f21de57`, with the archived source patch; Mooncake 0.3.12.post1, RDMA, shared master, reader `global_segment_size=0`, 128 MiB local buffers and 8 GiB per writer/publisher. Use 1 and 4 deployments, 32 HTTP threads/deployment, and 1/4 native reader clients as separate cases. Reset prefix cache before each repetition and exclude warmup; aggregate throughput by the whole workload time span. The Slurm recipe and raw logs are currently cluster-local, not a portable public benchmark. These frozen-image runs precede the latest mechanical cleanup; they are not a fresh GPU measurement of the final PR head. Latest cleanup removes repeated per-output block-size metadata, uses the Scheduler's authoritative hash granularity and shares output construction between backends. Changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) passes. Latest focused rerun: **107 passed, 173 deselected**: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short ``` ## Profiling follow-up (2026-09-22) Same frozen runtime and 256K/four-turn workload as above, one DP4 deployment, 32 concurrent conversations, cross-host RDMA retrieval with four native readers. Each backend has two unprofiled controls and one profiled run (Slurm 29958.60). Mean control throughput: **SHM 0.596435 vs Mooncake 0.743928 request-turns/s (+24.7%)**. Mean workload duration: 214.65s vs 172.07s; about 95% of the time saved is in the three warm/prefix-reuse turns. This compares complete delivery paths, not intrinsic RDMA versus shared-memory read speed. Mean per-request Mooncake costs over 192 warm requests in the two controls: | Stage | Wall time | | --- | ---: | | Native batch get, including lookup/transfer/wait | 526 ms | | Copy buffers to bytes and release handles | 36.5 ms | | Final bytes concatenation | 10.2 ms | | Whole get_concatenated, including the above | 578 ms | | Separate per-client lock wait | 1486 ms | SHM materializes R3, encodes NumPy/Base64 and sends it through HTTP; Mooncake returns keys and fetches raw bytes separately. Mean warm-request HTTP completion is 17.88s vs 4.26s; post-HTTP retrieval/decoding/checking is 1.84s vs 2.45s. Mooncake therefore adds post-HTTP work but saves substantially more on HTTP delivery. For 128 profiled requests, the client HTTP read chain consumes 97.49 vs 6.28 CPU seconds, JSON decoding 8.23 vs 0.77; SHM also spends 14.04 CPU seconds on Base64 decoding. HTTP body volume is 11.61 GB vs 0.89 GB, with Mooncake still fetching another 8.71 GB of raw R3. The dominant observed saving is avoiding the large Python HTTP/JSON/Base64 path, not eliminating data transfer or concatenation. Mooncake publication/flush waiting is higher; not every stage is faster. Profile timings are inclusive CPU totals, not additive request latency. Profiling reduces throughput by 11.8% (SHM) and 3.3% (Mooncake); the table and throughput comparison use unprofiled controls. Native API time is not pure RDMA wire time, and exported function profiles do not fully account for native CPU. The SHM after-control used a restarted, re-warmed server after a profiler-export failure. These two controls are not a confidence interval. All six phases passed 768 request checks and 576 cached-prefix R3 equality checks, with identical prefix-hit counts and zero preemptions. This retains the fixed-token/model-weight, memory-capacity and frozen-image limitations above; it does not establish model quality or cross-backend bitwise equality. Raw profiles, controls and recipes are archived cluster-locally. ## Independent Aux configuration (2026-09-22) AuxOutput now requires `VLLM_AUX_OUTPUT_MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`; KV retains `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`. There is no implicit fallback. Both variables may explicitly point to the same file. The existing config class and native setup are reused; no new RPC, thread or abstraction is introduced. Worker, EngineCore publisher and external helper readers use the same Aux factory. Ray propagates the variable, not the file; the path must be readable on each relevant node. KV-specific `enable_offload` does not restrict Aux initialization, including when both variables explicitly select the same file. The initial configuration-isolation commit touched five files (+90/-9). The follow-up below removes the standalone document and corrects its erroneous offload restriction; those initial counts do not describe the final PR. Validation: **159 distinct local tests passed** and changed-file pre-commit (including configured mypy) passed: ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/test_ray_env.py tests/test_ray_env_utils.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_worker.py -k config -q --tb=short ``` A new GB200 run (Slurm step 29958.61) passed **32 request-turns and 16 cached-prefix R3 equality checks** across two independent DP4 deployments and opposite-node RDMA readers. Both containers inherited a KV config path pointing to a nonexistent file; valid writer/reader configs were supplied only through the new Aux variable. Workload: 32K initial prompt, eight conversations per deployment, two growing turns, 16 output tokens, async scheduling and chunked prefill. Keys-only responses, full R3 shape/dtype, token counts and cached-prefix equality passed; each instance recorded 260096 prefix-hit tokens and zero preemptions. This freshly tests the config patch on the pinned-image Python port described above, not a rebuild of the current full PR head. It is not a throughput A/B, model-quality evaluation, concurrent KV-connector traffic test or full Ray-cluster test. KV compatibility and Ray environment propagation are covered locally. ## Audit fixes (2026-09-22) - Remove the Aux rejection of KV `enable_offload=true`; shared configuration remains valid. The field controls KV-specific load policy, not Aux storage. - Fix API-side string stops: publish accepted incremental keys internally for requests with string stops and accumulate them in OutputProcessor. Ordinary requests retain terminal publication; external HTTP still returns keys only at completion. This avoids finishing at the API before EngineCore sends keys. - Correct the Mooncake Worker test to exercise keys-only output, not only a swapped storage backend. Add a network-independent tokenizer regression that checks two-step R3 byte equality when the API stops and aborts EngineCore. - Remove `docs/features/aux_output_mooncake.md` and its code reference. Final local validation: **148 tests passed** (112 store/config/related Scheduler cases, 173 deselected; 36 TITO/IPC/collector cases). Changed-file pre-commit, including configured mypy, and `git diff --check` passed. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -k 'mooncake or aux or routed_experts or store' -q --tb=short HF_HUB_CACHE= HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_generate_stream.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_aux_output_keys_preserve_existing_output_wire_positions tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_terminal_aux_output_keys_survive_ipc_and_output_processing tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py::test_request_output_collector -q --tb=short ``` String-stop requests incur more small-object writes; that performance cost has not been measured. The GPU runs above predate these audit fixes and are not claimed as validation of the new string-stop path. No new GPU run was performed. ## Backend layout follow-up ```text aux_output_connector/ store.py Shared BlockObject, error and background writer shm.py ShmBlockObjectStore mooncake.py MooncakeBlockObjectStore and output publisher ``` Move the existing SHM implementation into its own module and update imports, type references and test patches. No new interface, RPC or thread. The split also removes a redundant `slot is None` guard in SHM `put`; it is not a class-name-only AST change. Two older Worker test fixtures now explicitly select the SHM backend. Validation: **107 store/config tests + 18 capture tests passed**; changed-file pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed. One additional capture test fails while importing the installed Humming dependency (`humming.dtypes.float4e0m3` missing). Running that test's original HEAD source reproduces the same failure; it is not counted as passing. No new GPU benchmark was run for this mechanical split. ```bash /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --tb=short /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py -q --tb=short ``` ## Mooncake PD + R3 handoff (2026-09-22) Enable `MooncakeConnector` with the Mooncake Aux backend. P runs the full prompt with `max_tokens=1` and no R3 prompt cropping; D receives the same prompt and the normal KV-transfer parameters plus: ```json "aux_output_prefix": {"block_size": 4, "keys": ["

", "

"]} ``` The block size is the R3/hash granularity (4 in this test), not the KV page size. D reuses shared full-block keys directly. Scheduler sends only the key for an unaligned first-forward boundary; Worker restores that block's missing prefix and joins newly computed R3. Aligned starts require no restore read. No full-prefix import or republication is needed. P objects remain immutable; the caller must keep source objects available. The configuration-level KV connector/PD blacklist has now been removed for both Aux backends. This is not a claim that every connector/backend implements remote R3 handoff; this PR's tested handoff is Mooncake PD + Mooncake Aux. Identical keys retain the first published value. After a cache miss and recomputation, returned R3 may therefore differ from the latest execution. This is an explicit accepted limitation; no overwrite or version mapping is introduced. Fresh tail keys can also wrap slices of older full objects. Validation: - 117 store/config tests passed; changed-file pre-commit, including mypy, passed. - Slurm 30373, two GB200 nodes, independent DP4/EP4 instances, real RDMA KV transfer and a shared Mooncake Store: all five cases passed. - Prompts 1025/1027/1028/1029/4099; D started at 1024/1026/1027/1028/4098. Covered 2–5 prefill chunks, streaming/nonstreaming, immutable P keys, complete external readback and later local reuse without the manifest. - First handoffs matched raw GPU rows exactly. Repeated keys retained their bytes; repackaged tails were checked against current or previously validated same-position rows, consistent with the first-writer contract. - Actual weights: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base. Same pinned image/Python adapter as above; modified Aux modules match the candidate source. This is not a full target-revision rebuild, throughput benchmark, or model-quality evaluation. - The initial retry oracle incorrectly assumed every new tail key represented new computation. Its failure logs were retained; the corrected checker and successful explicit retry are archived with the job. Slurm was cancelled after that retry passed, releasing both nodes. ```bash HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 /home/aoshen/vllm/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py -q --disable-warnings ``` AI assistance was used for this follow-up. Human review and acceptance of the semantic tradeoff and test evidence remain required before merge. ## Shared-key PD simplification (2026-09-23) Remove instance/DP namespaces and full-prefix restoration: production net **-28 lines**, touching only the two Aux connector modules and existing tests. No Scheduler/ModelRunner changes, new RPC or background-thread removal. Same P/D generation is an explicit deployment requirement. - **113 store/config tests passed**, changed-file pre-commit (including mypy) and `git diff --check` passed. Command is the store/config command above. - Independent Claude Opus 5.5 and Kimi K3 multi-round audits concluded APPROVE. - New Slurm **30589**, GB200 17/18, native RDMA: five PD cases passed with prompts 1025/1027/1028/1029/4099, 2–5 prefill chunks, streaming/nonstreaming, shared full-key equality, immutable P objects and later local cache reuse. D first-forward positions were 1024/1026/1027/1028/4098, confirming KV loading. - First checker failed on a later reuse: it only allowed the immediately prior response's R3, excluding an older valid first-writer row at the same position. The corrected checker allows previously validated same-position rows for new repackaged tails, while checking old-key immutability. Independent Kimi review approved the correction; the explicit rerun passed all five cases. Original failure logs remain: the batch retains exit 1 from the first checker; the rerun checker exited 0. No production patch was needed for this failure. - Actual weights: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base; existing pinned-image adapter, with changed modules byte-identical to this candidate. Not a full PR-image rebuild, throughput A/B or model-quality evaluation. Resources have been released. AI assistance was used. Human review remains required before merge. ## Main merge and PD policy (2026-09-23) Merged main (`88aa0d287d`) without force-push. Removed the entire AuxOutput KV connector blacklist, rather than keeping backend/connector exceptions. Other compatibility checks (model runner, PP/DCP/PCP, etc.) are unchanged. Configuration/store tests: **231 passed**; merge-file pre-commit passed. This permits configuration; it does not supply SHM with cross-host object access. Matched PD vs PD+R3 throughput completed successfully (Slurm **30597**, GB200 17/18, 20m13s). Same nodes, order PD -> PD+R3 -> PD, two measured rounds per phase; 64 requests/round, concurrency32, 32768 input +128 output tokens. Both P/D use DP4/EP4, async scheduling and real Mooncake RDMA KV transfer. | Mode | HTTP output tokens/s | Including full R3 retrieval | | --- | ---: | ---: | | PD, pooled before/after | 232.506 | 232.506 | | PD+R3 | 230.966 | 230.590 | | Change | -0.66% | -0.82% | Startup/warmup excluded. Each of the six measured rounds recorded2097152 external-KV hit tokens and zero P/D preemptions. All384 measured requests passed token checks;128 R3 requests passed full key-readback size checks, fetching1.086GB total. Raw-position correctness is covered by the prior E2E, not by this throughput checker. Four reader clients fetch R3 after HTTP; thread slots remain occupied through retrieval, so HTTP throughput is not an isolated model-execution metric. Before/after baseline drift was0.12%. Actual weights remain DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base, using the established frozen-image adapter, not a full latest-main rebuild. No raw GPU trace hooks, no MTP; synthetic cold prompts at one workload point. Few repeats are not a confidence interval. Resources released; user allocation14/15 untouched.

 For pipelining generation and training to improve GPU utilization and throughput, see the [Async Reinforcement Learning](async_rl.md) guide, which covers the pause/resume API for safely updating weights mid-flight.
 
+## Routed-expert outputs in Mooncake
+
+`--aux-output-config '{"enable_return_routed_experts":true,"backend":"mooncake"}'`
+stores routed-expert (R3) data in Mooncake and returns ordered `aux_output_keys`
+on the terminal `/inference/v1/generate` response. Configure the backend with
+`VLLM_AUX_OUTPUT_MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`; it is independent of KV transfer configuration.
+
+- Share a namespace only between instances using the same weights, R3 profile
+  (layers, experts per token and dtype), block size, hash settings and reset
+  generation. Generation starts at zero again after a process restart; it does
+  not identify a checkpoint. Use a separate Store or a separate Mooncake tenant
+  for each model/checkpoint/profile cohort, and rotate the tenant when restarting
+  with different weights. P and D must use the same cohort.
+- Tenant isolation requires **both** `tenant_id` in the client JSON and
+  `--enable_multi_tenants=true` on the Mooncake master with a registered tenant
+  quota. Without that master setting, different client tenant IDs share the
+  default namespace. See [Mooncake tenant configuration](https://kvcache-ai.github.io/Mooncake/deployment/mooncake-store-deployment-guide.html#tenant-quota-management).
+- Retention is owned by the deployment. Size the pool for outstanding outputs
+  and all consumers' read delays. An embedded client's contributed memory lasts
+  only as long as that storage participant; use separately managed Store nodes
+  when outputs must outlive vLLM processes.
+- Response-tail keys (`r3-tail:`) are outside the `vllm-artifact/` full-block
+  namespace. Include both prefixes in ACL, quota and cleanup policies. There is
+  no automatic tail TTL or consumer reference count. After **all** readers,
+  including any P/D handoff, finish, the owner may reclaim its tail keys with
+  the native client's `remove(key)`. Do not delete shared full-block keys when
+  one request or trainer finishes. Without explicit cleanup, tails remain until
+  Store eviction or loss of their storage replicas.
+
 See the following notebooks showing how to use vLLM for GRPO:
 
 - [Efficient Online Training with GRPO and vLLM in TRL](https://huggingface.co/learn/cookbook/grpo_vllm_online_training)

+def test_mooncake_pd_reads_only_boundary_and_reuses_shared_blocks(

+    full_end = prompt_length // _BLOCK_SIZE * _BLOCK_SIZE
+    source_keys = [f"prefill-{i}" for i in range(0, prompt_length, _BLOCK_SIZE)]
+    source_keys[: full_end // _BLOCK_SIZE] = routed_experts_keys(
+        hashes[: full_end // _BLOCK_SIZE], "0"
+    )
+    objects = [
+        BlockObject(key, source[i : i + _BLOCK_SIZE].tobytes())
+        for key, i in zip(source_keys, range(0, prompt_length, _BLOCK_SIZE))
+    ]
+    remote_store.put(objects)
+    worker = _make_worker(1)
+    worker._store.close()
+    worker._store = BackgroundBlockObjectStore(remote_store, max_pending_batches=2)
+    worker._return_keys = True
+    step = _metadata(
+        0,
+        [_request_metadata("decode", prompt_length - 1, 13 - prompt_length, 0, hashes)],
+        {},
+    )
+    if (prompt_length - 1) % _BLOCK_SIZE:
+        step.metadata.remote_tails["decode"] = source_keys[
+            (prompt_length - 1) // _BLOCK_SIZE
+        ]
+    remote_store._store.put_batch.reset_mock()
+    output = _process_output(
+        worker, step, rows[prompt_length - 1 :], ["decode"], np.array([0])

+    boundary = (prompt_length - 1) // _BLOCK_SIZE

+    )

+        for key in call.args[0]
+    }

+    assert remote_store.get_concatenated(source_keys) == source.tobytes()

+"""Immutable auxiliary-output blocks in a deployment-managed Mooncake Store."""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from itertools import groupby
+from math import prod
+from typing import TYPE_CHECKING, Any, cast
+from uuid import uuid4
+
+if TYPE_CHECKING:
+    from vllm.distributed.aux_output_connector.connector import AuxRequestOutput
+    from vllm.v1.request import Request

+    BlockObject,
+    BlockObjectStoreError,
+)
+
+
+class MooncakeBlockObjectStore:
+    """Use native owned-buffer I/O; publication runs on the shared writer thread.
+
+    Retention belongs to the deployment, not individual vLLM requests. Missing
+    objects fail closed; releasing a request never deletes external objects.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, store: Any, *, object_nbytes: int, max_batch_bytes: int) -> None:
+        if not 0 < object_nbytes <= max_batch_bytes:
+            raise ValueError("Mooncake batch must fit at least one auxiliary block")
+        self._store = store
+        self.object_nbytes = object_nbytes
+        self._batch_size = max_batch_bytes // object_nbytes
+
+    def put(
+        self,
+        objects: list[BlockObject],
+        *,
+        retain_keys: Iterable[str] = (),
+        release_keys: Iterable[str] = (),
+    ) -> None:
+        unique = {obj.key: obj.payload for obj in objects}
+        keys = list(unique)
+        for start in range(0, len(keys), self._batch_size):
+            batch_keys = keys[start : start + self._batch_size]
+            values = [unique[key] for key in batch_keys]
+            if any(not 0 < len(value) <= self.object_nbytes for value in values):
+                raise ValueError("Mooncake object exceeds auxiliary block capacity")
+            result = self._store.put_batch(batch_keys, values)
+            if result != 0:
+                raise BlockObjectStoreError(f"Mooncake publication failed: {result}")
+
+    def get_concatenated(self, keys: list[str]) -> bytes:
+        chunks = []
+        for start in range(0, len(keys), self._batch_size):
+            batch_keys = keys[start : start + self._batch_size]
+            buffers = self._store.batch_get_buffer(batch_keys)
+            for key, buffer in zip(batch_keys, buffers, strict=True):
+                if buffer is None:
+                    raise BlockObjectStoreError(f"Mooncake object unavailable: {key}")
+                chunks.append(bytes(buffer))
+            # Release native handles before the next batch uses the local pool.
+            del buffer, buffers
+        return b"".join(chunks)
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self._store.close()
+
+
+class MooncakeOutputPublisher:
+    """Finalize accepted boundary bytes without reading complete output blocks."""
+
+    def __init__(self, output: "AuxRequestOutput", block_size: int) -> None:
+        self._block_size = block_size
+        self._row_nbytes = prod(output.rows.shape[1:]) * output.rows.dtype.itemsize
+        self._store = create_mooncake_block_store(
+            object_nbytes=block_size * self._row_nbytes
+        )
+        self._chunks: dict[str, list[str | bytes]] = {}
+
+    def take_output(
+        self, request: "Request", output: "AuxRequestOutput"
+    ) -> list[str] | None:
+        start, end = output.token_start, request.num_tokens - 1
+        if end < start:
+            assert not request.is_finished()
+            return None
+        keys = output.block_keys
+        assert keys is not None
+        block_size = self._block_size
+        stored_start = start // block_size * block_size
+        stored_end = stored_start + len(keys) * block_size if keys else start
+        assert end <= stored_end + len(output.rows)
+        chunks = self._chunks.setdefault(request.request_id, [])
+        for index, key in enumerate(keys):
+            block_start = stored_start + index * block_size
+            lo, hi = max(start, block_start), min(end, block_start + block_size)
+            if hi <= lo:
+                break
+            if lo == block_start and hi == block_start + block_size:
+                chunks.append(key)
+            else:
+                payload = self._store.get_concatenated([key])
+                chunks.append(
+                    payload[
+                        (lo - block_start) * self._row_nbytes : (hi - block_start)
+                        * self._row_nbytes
+                    ]
+                )
+        if end > stored_end:
+            chunks.append(output.rows[: end - stored_end].tobytes())
+        # String stops are detected in the API process, which needs these keys
+        # before it can finish the request and abort the EngineCore request.
+        assert request.sampling_params is not None
+        if not request.is_finished() and not request.sampling_params.stop:
+            return None
+        del self._chunks[request.request_id]
+        result: list[str] = []
+        objects = []
+        for is_key, group in groupby(chunks, lambda chunk: isinstance(chunk, str)):
+            if is_key:
+                result.extend(cast(Iterable[str], group))
+            else:
+                payload = b"".join(cast(Iterable[bytes], group))
+                object_nbytes = self._store.object_nbytes
+                for offset in range(0, len(payload), object_nbytes):
+                    key = f"r3-tail:{uuid4().hex}"
+                    result.append(key)
+                    objects.append(
+                        BlockObject(key, payload[offset : offset + object_nbytes])
+                    )
+        self._store.put(objects)
+        return result
+
+    def discard(self, request_id: str) -> None:
+        self._chunks.pop(request_id, None)
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self._store.close()

+            max_batch_bytes=min(max_batch_bytes, config.local_buffer_size),
+        )

**[P1] Full-block keys are not unique across models, weights or restarts**

Complete-block keys are `vllm-artifact/{generation}/{block_hash}` (`worker.py:436`, `routed_experts.py:165`). Neither part identifies the producer:
- With the default `sha256` and no `PYTHONHASHSEED`, `resolve_none_hash_seed` returns the fixed `"vllm-none-hash"` (`kv_cache_utils.py:117-122`). Identical token sequences therefore hash identically in every process, across restarts, and across models.
- `generation` is a per-process counter that starts at 0 (`connector.py:57`).
- The Mooncake store is deployment-owned and outlives vLLM, and an existing key keeps its first value.

Failure scenario: an RL job restarts vLLM from a newer checkpoint. Generation is 0 again, so the first prompt publishes `vllm-artifact/0/<h>`, which already exists from the previous run, and the response returns that key. The trainer replays routing computed with the old weights, with no error. The same happens when two deployments share one store, for example two checkpoints of one model, or two models with the same tokenizer. With a different layer count, top-k or expert-ID dtype, the object size does not even match.

Suggestion: make the namespace explicit and collision-free:
- a required deployment namespace, which operators rotate per weight version;
- the R3 profile in the key: `num_layers`, `top_k`, dtype and hash block size.

The first-writer limitation in the description covers nondeterministic recomputation under the same weights. It should not extend to different weights or different models.

- **Without `aux_output_prefix`:** `build_connector_meta` raises `ValueError` (`connector.py:82`).

Any exception in the step reaches `EngineCore encountered a fatal error` (`core.py:1508`), so every in-flight request fails. The description says this "does not supply SHM with cross-host object access", but the result is a crash, not an unsupported feature.

Please keep rejecting P/D connectors when `backend == "shm"`, and allow them only with the Mooncake backend.

**[P1] String-stop requests publish one never-deleted, single-row object per generated token, synchronously on the EngineCore thread**

For requests with `sampling_params.stop`, `take_output` finalizes on every call (`mooncake.py:115`). Each decode step therefore does one blocking `put_batch` from `Scheduler.update_from_output` and creates a new `r3-tail:<uuid>` object that holds only that step's row.

A CPU probe drove this class with a fake native store, block size 4, an 8-token prompt and 100 decode steps:

| | sync `put_batch` calls | tail objects | returned keys |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| no string stops | 1 | 25 | 27 |
| with string stops | 100 | 100 | 102 |

Consequences for an RL rollout of several thousand tokens with stop strings:
- thousands of RDMA writes per request on the scheduling thread;
- thousands of small objects that are never deleted;
- thousands of separate reads for the trainer.

The description says this cost "has not been measured", and the GPU runs used 16-128 output tokens.

Suggestion: keep the accumulation path for string-stop requests too, and finalize once when the API-side stop fires. This is the same accepted-range finalization my earlier comment on abort asks for.

`MooncakeOutputPublisher` is created lazily on the first Mooncake output. `setup_mooncake_store` therefore runs inside `update_from_output` while requests are being served. It connects to the master and registers a segment, which the description sizes at 8 GiB for the publisher.

**[P2] Per-response tail objects have no deletion path**

Full-block keys are shared, so leaving their retention to the deployment is reasonable. `r3-tail:<uuid>` objects, however, belong to exactly one response, yet nothing ever deletes them, and the caller has no way to signal that it has read them.

Reclamation relies entirely on Mooncake eviction. Eviction can drop shared full blocks that later prefix hits still need, while dead tails stay resident. Combined with the string-stop finding, this grows by one object per token.

At minimum, document that the pool must hold every tail until it is evicted. Preferably, give tails a lease or TTL, or a consumer-side release.

D requires `kv_transfer_params["aux_output_prefix"]` for every new request with `num_external_cached_tokens > 0`. However, the only places that construct it are the unit tests (`test_store.py:252,257`):

Please either have P return the manifest in its `kv_transfer_params` (block size and ordered keys) and have the reference proxy forward it, or document the caller contract and fail the request, not the engine, when it is absent.

**[P2] A missing or evicted remote object kills the engine instead of failing the request**

With the Mooncake backend, eviction is decided by the Mooncake master under pool pressure, which can come from other tenants of a shared store, not by this vLLM instance. When a read finds an object gone, this `BlockObjectStoreError` propagates out of the engine step:
- the worker's `_restore_tail` (`worker.py:334`) raises on the output thread, inside `process_output`;
- the EngineCore publisher's boundary read (`mooncake.py:103`) raises inside `Scheduler.update_from_output`.

Both reach `EngineCore encountered a fatal error` (`core.py:1508`), so every in-flight request fails because one object was evicted.

For SHM, failing closed on a local eviction is a capacity misconfiguration the operator controls. For a shared store, it should fail only the affected request (finish it with an error, or recompute the boundary as the KV failed-load path does).

+        self.object_nbytes = object_nbytes
+        self._batch_size = max_batch_bytes // object_nbytes
+
+    def put(
+        self,
+        objects: list[BlockObject],
+        *,
+        retain_keys: Iterable[str] = (),
+        release_keys: Iterable[str] = (),
+    ) -> None:
+        unique = {obj.key: obj.payload for obj in objects}
+        keys = list(unique)
+        for start in range(0, len(keys), self._batch_size):
+            batch_keys = keys[start : start + self._batch_size]
+            values = [unique[key] for key in batch_keys]
+            if any(not 0 < len(value) <= self.object_nbytes for value in values):
+                raise ValueError("Mooncake object exceeds auxiliary block capacity")
+            result = self._store.put_batch(batch_keys, values)
+            if result != 0:
+                raise BlockObjectStoreError(f"Mooncake publication failed: {result}")
+
+    def get_concatenated(self, keys: list[str]) -> bytes:
+        chunks = []
+        for start in range(0, len(keys), self._batch_size):
+            batch_keys = keys[start : start + self._batch_size]
+            buffers = self._store.batch_get_buffer(batch_keys)
+            for key, buffer in zip(batch_keys, buffers, strict=True):
+                if buffer is None:
+                    raise BlockObjectStoreError(f"Mooncake object unavailable: {key}")
+                chunks.append(bytes(buffer))
+            # Release native handles before the next batch uses the local pool.
+            del buffer, buffers
+        return b"".join(chunks)
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        self._store.close()
+
+
+class MooncakeOutputPublisher:
+    """Finalize accepted boundary bytes without reading complete output blocks."""
+
+    def __init__(self, output: "AuxRequestOutput", block_size: int) -> None:
+        self._block_size = block_size
+        self._row_nbytes = prod(output.rows.shape[1:]) * output.rows.dtype.itemsize
+        self._store = create_mooncake_block_store(
+            object_nbytes=block_size * self._row_nbytes
+        )
+        self._chunks: dict[str, list[str | bytes]] = {}
+
+    def take_output(
+        self, request: "Request", output: "AuxRequestOutput"
+    ) -> list[str] | None:
+        start, end = output.token_start, request.num_tokens - 1
+        if end < start:
+            assert not request.is_finished()
+            return None
+        keys = output.block_keys
+        assert keys is not None
+        block_size = self._block_size
+        stored_start = start // block_size * block_size
+        stored_end = stored_start + len(keys) * block_size if keys else start
+        assert end <= stored_end + len(output.rows)
+        chunks = self._chunks.setdefault(request.request_id, [])
+        for index, key in enumerate(keys):
+            block_start = stored_start + index * block_size
+            lo, hi = max(start, block_start), min(end, block_start + block_size)
+            if hi <= lo:
+                break
+            if lo == block_start and hi == block_start + block_size:
+                chunks.append(key)
